newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain trade deficit widens in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain trade deficit widens in first quarter.

text.p: MANAMA, July 2 (Rueter) - Bahrain's foreign trade deficit rose to 99.8 million dinars ($264.7 million) in the first quarter of 1997, up from 97.8 million dinars a year earlier, official figures showed.
The Central Statistics Organisation said Bahrain exported goods worth 128.1 million dinars in the first quarter of 1997 and imported goods worth 227.9 million dinars.
Last year, Bahrain's exports in the first three months stood at 121.7 million dinars and its imports totalled 219.5 million dinars, the statistics showed.
Bahrain's main exports are oil, gas and aluminium.

Bahrain, the least wealthy Gulf Arab state, is a small independent oil producer. It produces around 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) from its own fields and receives the entire 140,000 bpd from an offshore field shared with neighbour Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom was the main destination for Bahraini exports in both periods, importing goods worth 19.63 million dinars from Bahrain between January and March 1997. In first quarter 1996 Bahrain exported to Saudi Arabia goods worth 25.26 million.
Bahrain's other main export markets are India, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

The United States was the major source of imports into the island state in the first three months of this year. Bahrain imported U.S. goods worth 24.08 million versus 24.4 million dinars in the same period last year.
Other important sources for imports into Bahrain were Australia, Britain, Japan and Saudi Arabia.
